members.title: Gulf nations on alert after US strikes Iranian island
members.lead: Kuwait said on Wednesday it was countering “hostile drone attacks”, as Washington’s Gulf allies remained on alert hours after the United States struck Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Bahrain said its air defences intercepted attacks from Iran early Wednesday, a day after Tehran’s Revolutionary Guards said they attacked a base in the country used by Washington. The interceptions come as the United States and Iran remain in a standoff over the key waterway, a conduit for global energy shipments, despite a lull in the war triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February. The conflict has spilled over to Gulf states that host US military facilities, as Tehran stepped up retaliatory attacks. Kuwait’s military said Wednesday its air defences were “responding to hostile drone threats”, urging its public to follow security and safety advice. . Earlier, Iran’s official IRNA news agency cited a regional official as saying the United States had hit Qeshm Island without causing serious damage. US fighter jets “used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island”, an American official told AFP on condition of anonymity, adding that the strike was in response to Iranian “aggression targeting US personnel and assets”. Washington and Tehran have vied for control over the Hormuz strait, with the US military working to protect ships transiting the waterway in defiance of Iran’s attempts to close it. . Despite Washington and Tehran holding back from a full resumption of hostilities, tensions remain high. On Tuesday, US President Donald Trump said he was taking “very seriously” reports that Iran was developing plans to use a so-called “dirty bomb” in Washington. CNN cited seven anonymous US officials as saying Iran was plotting how to target senior administration figures with a bomb laced with chemical or radioactive material, though they stopped short of saying Iran planned to carry out such an attack.…

members.title: Apec summit live: Xi and Putin give opening speeches as world leaders gather in China
members.lead: We’re back for day two of the Apec CEO Summit in China’s southern tech hub of Shenzhen. Today the summit will be addressed by APEC leaders, with President Xi Jinping set to give a keynote speech. Bilateral meetings will continue on the sidelines, although the most eye-catching – Xi and Donald Trump, and the US-China-Russia trilateral – won’t be until Thursday. Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen this morning, greeted by a red carpet, soldiers and pom pom-waving dancers dressed in fuchsia and blue. Communist party politburo member Cai Qi, often described as Xi’s right-hand man, was there to meet him. Trump will leave Manila, where he has been attending the Asean forum, later on Wednesday. members.title: Xi, Putin meet ahead of historic Trump trilateral summit
members.lead: Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin began talks in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a day ahead of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump in the southern Chinese city. Thursday’s trilateral has triggered fears that the three powerful men could decide the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe, and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence. Washington had signalled that Ukraine -- something Xi vehemently sees as not China’s problem -- was not expected to be addressed, before Trump said that it would. China has said only that the leaders would hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations” on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting. . Also up for discussion are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February. Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile. . Chinese and Russian news agencies reported at around noon on Wednesday that Xi and Putin had met for talks -- the fifth time the two leaders have met this year, including once by video link. Putin has been shunned by the West since launching Europe’s worst conflict since World War II with his 2022 attack on Ukraine. Addressing the APEC gathering on Wednesday, he said he expected the trilateral summit with Xi and Trump to be “highly useful”. . China has said only that the leaders would hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations” on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting. . “At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is unity rather than division... and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” Putin said.
